q: I archived /lab/work/project by its full path and extracted it in /tmp/restore. Where are my files?
expl: Tar keeps the whole path, minus the leading slash. Use -C with the parent folder to get short paths.

q: How can I prove an archive still matches the files on disk?
expl: gzip -t only checks the compression. tar -d compares every file, and prints nothing when they match.

q: You can be in any folder. Type a `tar` command that creates `/tmp/backup.tgz` from `/lab/work/project` with short paths that start with `project/`.
expl: `-C /lab/work` changes into the parent folder first, so the archive stores `project/...` instead of `lab/work/project/...`.

q: tar printed the warning "Removing leading '/' from member names". Later you extract that archive with `tar -xzf` inside an empty folder `/tmp/x`. What happens to the original folder?
expl: Removing the slash makes the paths relative, so extracting is safe; you just get the files several folders deep.
opts: It's overwritten with the archived copies
Nothing: the files land in `/tmp/x/...` with the full path inside
tar refuses to extract an archive made from an absolute path

q: Type the command that lists what's inside `small.tgz`, without extracting anything.
expl: `-t` lists the contents. GNU tar also detects gzip by itself when reading, so `-tf` works too.
ch: Create an archive and look inside

q: `small.tgz` was made with `--exclude=node_modules --exclude='*.log'`. What does this print?
expl: `'*.log'` skips the log file, but the empty `logs/` folder is still stored. `node_modules` is gone completely.

q: You type `tar -cfz backup.tgz project`. What happens?
expl: The `f` option takes the next word as the archive name. Keep `f` last: `-czf backup.tgz`.
ch: Create an archive and look inside
opts: tar writes to a file named `z`, because the file name must come right after `f`

expl: tar names the file and says what differs. Here the new text is one byte longer, so the size changed as well as the time.

q: `/tmp/one` is an empty folder. Type a command that extracts only `project/README.md` from `small.tgz` into it.
expl: Give the path exactly as `tar -t` lists it, and tar extracts only that file.

expl: `-C` is "change directory". The archive is still written where you named it, here `good.tgz` in the current folder.
